decision: v1.2 (2026-07-31) — the sticky-incumbent swap test is now BAND-AWARE. It compared raw EV while the ranking uses (odds, band, EV), so an incumbent could hold a slot while ranking WORSE on the canonical key, and hold it on the one metric this ledger shows is ANTI-predictive. Live case: DiLeo (band 0, odds 1.9091, EV 0.213) could not displace Carleton (band 1, odds 1.9804, EV 0.462), so the card kept a TIER B play over a TIER A one — and Carleton only held the slot because she was carded at 04:08, before the v1.1 correlation-cap fix. Stickiness was protecting the output of the bug v1.1 corrected. A challenger now displaces when it is better ON THE BAND (structural, and band membership barely moves during a slate, so it cannot churn); within the same band the original SWAP_MARGIN EV rule is unchanged, preserving the anti-churn property that stickiness exists for (57% of pools once carded more than the two plays a card holds). Tier records behind the ordering: A 14-3 / 82.4% / +0.73u per bet vs B 17-11 / 60.7% / +0.20u. RESTATEMENT COST: the counted record moves 33-15 / +19.05u to 33-16 / +18.05u — one additional graded loss enters as a different incumbent yields. Reported, not hidden.

wnba_slip._SCHEMA:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS parlays(
  pred_date TEXT, key TEXT, legs TEXT, n INTEGER, dec REAL, ev REAL,
  result TEXT, pnl REAL, played INTEGER DEFAULT 0, graded INTEGER DEFAULT 0, graded_at TEXT,
  UNIQUE(pred_date, key));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS selections (
    pred_date TEXT, team TEXT, player TEXT, stat TEXT, selected_at TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (pred_date, team, player, stat))
